target_customer: Small and mid sized US trucking fleets and owner operators that run their own dispatch
problem: Dispatchers spend their day finding loads, negotiating with brokers by phone, managing drivers and chasing paperwork, which limits how many trucks one dispatcher can run.
business_model: Subscription for AI dispatch agents ($99 first month, then from $349 per month per the company site)

founders.name: Eduardo Narvaez
founders.background_notes: Family trucking business of 20+ years per company site; YC page also lists environmental economics and supply chain emissions work with the Caixa Bank Foundation, Generalitat of Catalunya and Club of Rome.

founders.name: Hugo Alvarez
prior_employers: J&H Trucking (operations manager, now runs it)
founders.background_notes: Family roots in trucking per YC page and company site.

technical_complexity.rationale: The current product combines load board scraping, voice negotiation and document processing agents. Such a stack is feasible with current LLM tooling; what the company built in 2021 is not documented.

defensibility.rationale: Several funded rivals sell AI dispatch and the underlying models are shared; the family's trucking operating experience is the main differentiator.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not applicable at founding; by 2025 funded AI dispatch entrants such as FleetWorks ($17M) and TruckSmarter ($16M) appeared, per freight press.

market_need_then: Not documented for 2021. The company site now cites dispatcher workload and the YC page cites a family with over 20 years in trucking.

branding.domain_note: Uses tiriel.ai, an exact name on .ai.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and punchy, short contrasting fragments, trucking framing, English and Spanish mixed (company site)

branding.brand_signature: Pitch line: Don't buy dispatch software. Hire a dispatch team.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinctive coined name and a clear voice on the company site, but no press or community evidence about the brand.

outcome_analysis: Tiriel is a small, family run freight dispatch company that joined YC in Summer 2021 and today sells AI dispatch agents with a 10 person team. No funding amounts, exit or failure were found, and it is not clear what the product was in 2021, so the record shows an active company with unknown traction rather than a clear success or failure.
notes: The company site lists backers Y Combinator, Soma Capital, JAM Fund, Harvard University, Act One Ventures and AngelHub, but no amounts or dates, and searches for Soma, Act One and JAM found no Tiriel investment press; therefore no rounds are recorded. Competitor list left empty because no dated source about freight dispatch rivals near the 2021 batch was found; the products described on the YC page and site appear to be recent (AI agent framing), so what Tiriel built in 2021 is unknown. Narvaez education is as stated on the company site (finance degree, school not given). Name origin not found.
